A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WIRE research, despite the changed title and organization. All 18 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v3, including their appendices, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic-task, point-cloud, and graph-benchmark experiments, including additional architecture comparisons and an attention-pattern analysis in Appendix B.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds evaluations on two OGB datasets and experiments using random-walk positional features.

M1.justification: The core spectral WIRE algorithm and Performer integration remain unchanged. V3 removes the auxiliary stochastic Laplacian-diagonalization algorithm from v1 Appendix A.2 and concretely instantiates the random-walk feature option in Appendix A.6; v1 had already suggested random-walk inputs as a possible generalization.

E1.justification: V3 adds actual evaluations on ogbg-ppa and ogbg-code2 in Table 3 and Appendix A.4, retaining all earlier datasets and tasks. The added RWPE experiments reuse existing tasks. The PDFs provide limited descriptions of the two new datasets, so finer claims about their task or domain coverage are not supported.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain their comparator sets: no-WIRE controls, NoPE and Cartesian RoPE for point clouds, and the existing softmax, Performer, SGFormer, and BigBird comparisons. The additional studies reuse these comparison designs; newly cited methods such as FastRP and SignNet are not added as competing baselines in the reported tables.

E3.justification: The added RWPE shortest-path experiment uses 100 training epochs and supplies RWPEs as both absolute features and rotation inputs; the retained spectral experiment still uses 250 epochs. V3 also specifies evaluation settings for the added OGB datasets. Existing splits, metrics, and hyperparameter tables are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: V3 Appendix A.6 adds a feature-choice analysis testing whether WIRE gains persist with random-walk coordinates, using a shortest-path dimensionality sweep and five graph benchmarks. The earlier spectral sweeps, fixed-weight attention on/off illustration, and architecture ablations remain.

E5.justification: V3 Appendix A.4 adds ten-seed reporting for ogbg-ppa and six-seed reporting for ogbg-code2. Previously reported experiments retain their run counts and uncertainty practices; these additions do not establish increased replication of the earlier results.

E6.justification: Matched earlier numerical results are unchanged. New baseline/WIRE scores include 0.8009(8)/0.804(2) on ogbg-ppa and 0.1731(9)/0.1733(9) on ogbg-code2 in v3 Table 3. Tables 10–11 add RWPE outcomes, including shortest-path RMSE 0.061(1) without WIRE versus 0.055(2) with ten coordinates. These are added settings, not revisions to the spectral results.

T1.justification: V1's unconditional permutation-equivariance Remark 1 becomes v3 Lemma 1 with explicit sign and degenerate-eigenspace ambiguities. V3 adds an argument for gauge invariance of the expected limiting transformation and qualifies the ordering of grid eigenmodes. It also removes the complete stochastic-diagonalization derivation from v1 Appendix A.2. The effective-resistance theorem and proof are retained, with the proof moved into the main text.

C1.justification: The central claims about graph rotary encodings, recovery of RoPE on grids, effective resistance, and empirical usefulness remain. V3 removes unconditional permutation equivariance from the abstract and qualifies that guarantee in Lemma 1, narrowing one advertised theoretical property.

C2.justification: V3 substantially develops the distinction between basis ambiguity in individual WIRE instances and gauge invariance of its expected limiting behavior, proposing learned tolerance to these ambiguities as an explanation of empirical success. It also explains how alternative features trade spectral guarantees for computational efficiency and interprets RWPE results as evidence of robustness to feature choice.

D1.justification: V3 adds the RWPE construction formula and implementation information for the new OGB experiments, including NVIDIA A100 80GB hardware and an optional 16-dimensional Laplacian positional encoding. Most new OGB hyperparameters are specified through a cited configuration rather than reproduced locally. Existing code-access information and retained hyperparameter tables are unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds focused positioning around SignNet and Laplacian canonization, RWPE/WavePE/FastRP, and established spectral approximation methods. It explicitly frames exceeding 1-WL expressivity as a sanity check shared with other models. References including Nakatsukasa, Raffel, and Wang are removed, while the central positioning as graph-compatible RoPE remains.

P1.justification: V3 changes the title and expands WIRE as Wave-Induced rather than Wavelet-Induced Rotary Encodings. It rewrites the abstract and introductory framing, reorganizes Section 3 into four subsections, moves the resistance proof into the main text, and consolidates point-cloud material in the appendix. The revision also introduces several incomplete cross-references.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column main text, relocates the schematic to the first page, and moves the point-cloud table into the appendix. It merges v1 Figures 3–4 into one synthetic-experiment figure, dropping one illustrative graph while retaining its evaluated condition. It adds RWPE Tables 10–11, expands the benchmark table, and changes proof text to gray.

improvement.justification: V3 improves scientific precision by qualifying the overbroad equivariance statement and adds useful validation of non-spectral WIRE and two further benchmarks. These gains are tempered by unequal training budgets in the spectral/RWPE shortest-path comparison, incomplete local documentation of the new benchmarks, and broken cross-references. The evidence supports a limited net improvement rather than a substantial overall advance.
